findings.reason: the plan must thread the machine through select_machine/ArtifactMachineSelector and say how JT-60SA identity resolves (a second registry or a machine-keyed lookup), which is a different open item from the authoring route it does flag (jt60sa-artifact-authoring) and is currently unnamed.
findings.text: §7 makes resolve_machine_description machine-keyed but leaves the spine's selection path MAST-pinned: ArtifactMachineSelector.select calls identity_for_shot (machine_identity.py:207, whose default_registry at :145 is nova.catalog.mast_geometry.MachineGeometryRegistry) and selects the artifact with no machine argument, and _read at machine_selection.py:172 calls read_acquisition_channels() with the default machine="mast" — so a JT-60SA shot raises MachineIdentityError at the registry select before the new pin table is ever consulted

findings.reason: with the week's interface budget at 0 across all four families, the section must either state what the added verdict surface retires or merges or why nothing can be, and the honest design is a unit-carrying reference verdict, or a scalar-equilibrium reference-scoring owner, rather than widening a metre-geometry referee.
findings.text: §7 adds q95 and Ip "as verdict components" to judge_geometry, whose GeometryVerdict (efit_referee.py:174) is documented geometry-in-metres with metre tolerances and whose passed verdict checks only axis/x-point/boundary; q95 is dimensionless and Ip is a current, so the two scalars would sit in the components dict unreported in passed and un-scored, mixing unit systems inside a module firewalled and named for EFIT reconstruction outputs

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the new modules are deep rather than wide: §3 lands one batch-fetch function and one cache writer behind which the ssh session, the msgpack array codec and the {shot}.zarr layout hide, and §2's exporter is one public function writing the directory from a catalogue and its signal maps.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan routes the JT-60SA description through gs/artifact_resolution.py's machine-keyed pin table, but the owner of "which machine is this shot" is gs/machine_selection.py ArtifactMachineSelector and gs/machine_identity.py identity_for_shot/default_registry, which are pinned to MAST and are not named as something to extend.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §7 adds q95 and Ip as new verdict components to the public judge_geometry interface without naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the plan searched both codebases it names and cites the mechanism each proposed piece extends (read_geometry_table, NetCDFTransformEngine, cocos_convention.score_conventions, challenge/convention._integrated_current, spine_bench.runner._magnetics_residual, gs/artifact_resolution.resolve_machine_description), and justifies the one parallel subsystem it adds (§3's extractor) against codex's existing remote layer (enumerate_edas.py / ssh_worker.py / serialization.py).
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the single layer the plan places over existing machinery without extending it (§3's extractor over codex's remote-execution layer) states why that machinery cannot be extended instead: importing it would make imas-codex's graph, LLM and tool-installation dependencies a dependency of every ambix read, which the map-persistence decision rules out.
